text: Transfers of personal data to a third country are allowed only on a lawful basis: an adequacy decision (Art. 45), appropriate safeguards such as standard contractual clauses (Art. 46), or a specific derogation (Art. 49). This is a reference summary for DPO review, not legal advice.

The European Commission can decide that a third country ensures an adequate level of data protection, allowing transfers without further safeguards. The set of adequate countries changes over time; always check the current list.

Third-party trackers and cookies may transfer identifiers and behavioural data to their operators. Consent and transparency obligations can apply. This is a reference note for review, not a compliance determination.
